sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.

Heard Mr. Prashant Kumar Singh, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.
Second supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for applicant in Court today is taken on record.

This application under section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed challenging order dated 16.5.2022, passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.1, Mathura in Case No. 4560 of 2017 (State VS.
C.M.D. Bappadatiya Majumdar and Others) under section 420, 506 IPC, arising out of Case Crime No. 940 of 2016, Police Station- Kotwali, District Mathura whereby application dated 6.4.2022 (paper no.18 B filed by applicant) for joint trial of Case No. 1346 of 2019 ( State VS. C.M.D.
Bappadatiya Majumdar and others) under sections 420 and 506 IPC, Police Station- Kotwali,
Smt. Manju Agarwal vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156548114/
1 District Mathura has been rejected.

sentences.text: Record shows that applicant who is also the first informant lodged an F.I.R. dated 29.9.2016, which was registered as Case Crime No. 940 of 2016, under sections 420 and 506 IPC, Police Station-Kotwali, District- Mathura.
In the aforesaid F.I.R. three persons namely respondents- 2, 3 and 4 have been nominated as named accused.

Investigating Officer after completion of statutory investigation of concerned case crime number,
submitted charge sheet dated 2.5.2017 whereby two of the named accused namely Bappadatiya Majumdar and Amit Kumar have been charge sheeted under section 420 and 506 IPC.
After submission of aforesaid charge sheet dated 2.5.2017, Cognizance was taken upon same by Court concerned vide Cognizance Taking Order dated 22.8.2017.
Resultantly, Criminal Case No. 4560 of 2017 (State VS. C.M.D. Bappadatiya Majumdar and Others) under section 420, 506 IPC, Police Station- Kotwali, District Mathura came to be registered.

entities.text: State VS. C.M.D. Bappadatiya Majumdar and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During pendency of aforementioned case, Investigating Officer submitted supplementary charge sheet dated 19.7.2017, whereby another named accused Ajay Kumar has been charge sheeted under sections 420 and 506 IPC.
After submission of aforesaid charge sheet, cognizance was taken upon same by Court concerned.
Resultantly Criminal Case No. 503 of 2018 (State Vs. Ajay Kumar) came to be registered.

entities.text: Criminal Case No. 503 of 2018 (State Vs. Ajay Kumar)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequently, applicant filed an application dated 6.4.2022, paper No. 18B purported to be under section 210 (2) Cr.P.C. for joint trial of aforesaid criminal cases.

However, Court below by means of impugned order has rejected the same, simply on the ground that in view of order dated 15.12.2021 passed by this Court, whereby Court below has been directed to dispose of one of the criminal case expeditiously preferably within a period of six months can not be complied with in case joint trial is directed.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that order impugned in present application is not only illegal but also arbitrary.

It is an undisputed fact that both the cases arise out of same case crime number,
therefore instead of registering another criminal case, on the basis of supplementary charge sheet.
Court below should have proceed against the subsequently charge sheeted accused in the criminal case already pending.
It is further submitted that application under section 210 (2) Cr.P.C. filed by applicant was not opposed by the prosecution.
However, Court below has rejected the application simply in view of order dated 15.12.2021, passed by this Court.
On the above primise, learned counsel for applicant submits that impugned order passed by Court below cannot be sustained and therefore, liable to be quashed by this Court.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. submits that in view of the peculiar facts of this case as noted herein above court below ought to have allowed the joint trial.
Order impugned cannot be sustained either in law or fact.

Having heard the learned Counsel for applicant and learned A.G.A for State and upon perusal of record, the Court finds that the two criminal cases referred to above arise out of same case crime Smt. Manju Agarwal vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156548114/
2 number.

entities.text: crime Smt. Manju Agarwal vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of above, documentary and oral evidence sought to be relied upon by the parteis shall be same.
There does not exist any such reason on the basis of which separate trial of aforementioned criminal case, can be sustained.
Moreover order impugned is contrary to the provisions contained in Section 210 (2) Cr.P.c.
In view of above, present application succeeds and is allowed.

Impugned order dated 16.5.2022,
passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.1, Mathura in Case No. 4560 of 2017 (State VS. C.M.D. Bappadatiya Majumdar and Others) under section 420, 506 IPC, arising out of Case Crime No. 940 of 2016, Police Station- Kotwali, District Mathura, is hereby quashed.
